def-stochastic-gradient-oracle-and-uncon:
## Definition

Fix a finite dimension $d\ge1$ and a discrete filtered probability space $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0},P)$ as in [[def-filtration-and-filtered-probability-space]]. A sequence $x_k:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d$ is an iterate process when each coordinate is $\mathcal F_k$-measurable; a sequence $G_k:\Omega\to\mathbb R^d$ is an oracle process when each coordinate is $\mathcal F_{k+1}$-measurable. These are coordinatewise instances of [[def-random-element-and-real-random-variable]] and [[def-adapted-and-integrable-stochastic-process]]. Assume the coordinates used in a conditional moment are square-integrable.

For deterministic stepsizes $\alpha_k>0$, the unconstrained Robbins–Monro/SGD update is
$$x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_kG_k.$$
For a differentiable objective $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$, the oracle is conditionally unbiased when $\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k)$ coordinatewise almost surely; it has conditional bias $b_k$ when $\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k)+b_k$. The conditional variance of a vector is the sum of the scalar conditional variances of its coordinates, using [[def-conditional-variance]]. By [[lem-conditional-variance-is-well-defined-and-has-the-second-moment-formula]], it satisfies
$$\mathbb E[\|G_k\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\|\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]\|_2^2+\operatorname{Var}(G_k\mid\mathcal F_k)$$
almost surely. All conditional expectations are coordinatewise instances of [[def-conditional-expectation-as-an-ae-class]], whose existence assumes the [[def-axiom-of-choice]]. No independence across iterations is part of this definition.

The conditional second-moment bound $\mathbb E[\|G_k\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le M_k^2$ and the conditional variance bound $\operatorname{Var}(G_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\le\sigma_k^2$ are distinct hypotheses; the latter combines with conditional unbiasedness through the displayed identity.
lem-robbins-siegmund-almost-supermarting:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,(\mathcal F_k)_{k\ge0},P)$ be a discrete filtered probability space. Let $X_k$ be nonnegative, adapted, and integrable for every $k$. Let $a_k,c_k$ be deterministic nonnegative sequences with finite sums, and let $b_k$ be nonnegative, $\mathcal F_k$-measurable, and integrable. If
$$\mathbb E[X_{k+1}\mid\mathcal F_k]\le(1+a_k)X_k-b_k+c_k\quad\text{almost surely for every }k,$$
then $X_k$ converges almost surely to a finite nonnegative random variable and $\sum_{k\ge0}b_k<\infty$ almost surely.
thm-robbins-monro-strongly-monotone-root:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $h:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R^d$ have a root $x^\ast$, so $h(x^\ast)=0$, and suppose that for some $\mu>0$,
$$\langle h(x)-h(y),x-y\rangle\ge\mu\|x-y\|_2^2\qquad(x,y\in\mathbb R^d).$$
On a filtered probability space, let $x_0$ be square-integrable and let $x_k,G_k$ follow [[def-stochastic-gradient-oracle-and-unconstrained-update]]. Assume each $h(x_k)$ is $\mathcal F_k$-measurable, and suppose
$$\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=h(x_k),\qquad \mathbb E[\|G_k\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le M^2$$
almost surely for a finite constant $M$. If the deterministic stepsizes satisfy $\alpha_k>0$, $\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty$, and $\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty$, then $x_k\to x^\ast$ almost surely. Strong monotonicity also makes the root unique.
thm-stochastic-gradient-nonconvex-random:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be continuously differentiable with $L$-Lipschitz gradient for $L>0$, and suppose $f(x)\ge f_{\inf}$ for every $x$, where $f_{\inf}\in\mathbb R$ is a lower bound. Let $x_0$ be deterministic, $\Delta=f(x_0)-f_{\inf}$, and run the unconstrained update of [[def-stochastic-gradient-oracle-and-unconstrained-update]] with constant $0<\alpha\le1/L$. Suppose
$$\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k),\qquad \operatorname{Var}(G_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\le\sigma^2$$
almost surely for every $k$. After generating $x_0,\ldots,x_{N-1}$, independently choose $R$ uniformly from $\{0,\ldots,N-1\}$ on the finite product extension of the trajectory space; equivalently, $\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x_R)\|_2^2=N^{-1}\sum_{k<N}\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2^2$. Then
$$\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x_R)\|_2^2\le\frac{2\Delta}{\alpha N}+L\alpha\sigma^2.$$
For fixed $\Delta,\sigma$, the stepsize $\alpha=\min\{1/L,\sqrt{2\Delta/(L\sigma^2N)}\}$ gives an $O(N^{-1/2})$ bound when $\Delta,\sigma>0$; zero cases have the stronger bounds specified in the proof. This is an optimization guarantee, not an inferential or central-limit theorem.
thm-stochastic-gradient-biased-noise-flo:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ have $L$-Lipschitz gradient for $L>0$ and satisfy $f(x)\ge f_{\inf}$ for a real lower bound $f_{\inf}$. Run the unconstrained update of [[def-stochastic-gradient-oracle-and-unconstrained-update]] from square-integrable $x_0$ with deterministic steps $0<\alpha_k\le1/(4L)$. Suppose
$$\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k)+b_k,\qquad \|b_k\|_2\le\beta_k,\qquad \operatorname{Var}(G_k\mid\mathcal F_k)\le\sigma_k^2$$
almost surely, where $b_k$ is $\mathcal F_k$-measurable and $\beta_k,\sigma_k$ are deterministic nonnegative bounds. For $N\ge1$ and $\Delta=\mathbb E f(x_0)-f_{\inf}<\infty$,
$$\frac{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2^2}{\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\alpha_k}\le \frac{2\Delta+2\sum_{k<N}\alpha_k\beta_k^2+2L\sum_{k<N}\alpha_k^2\beta_k^2+L\sum_{k<N}\alpha_k^2\sigma_k^2}{\sum_{k<N}\alpha_k}.$$
In particular, for constant $\alpha,\beta,\sigma$ the uniform average is at most
$$\frac{2\Delta}{\alpha N}+\frac52\beta^2+L\alpha\sigma^2,$$
and therefore
$$\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\mathbb E\|\nabla f(x_k)\|_2^2\le\frac52\beta^2+L\alpha\sigma^2.$$
Decreasing steps retain the displayed weighted bias and noise sums.
lem-strong-convexity-implies-strong-mono:
## Statement

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and convex, let $C\subseteq U$ be convex, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable. Suppose $f|_C$ is $\mu$-strongly convex in the strong-Jensen sense of [[def-strong-convex-composite-objective]], for $\mu>0$; explicitly, for $x,y\in C$ and $0<t<1$,
$$f((1-t)x+ty)\le(1-t)f(x)+tf(y)-\frac\mu2t(1-t)\|x-y\|_2^2.$$
Then for all $x,y\in C$,
$$f(y)\ge f(x)+\langle\nabla f(x),y-x\rangle+\frac{\mu}{2}\|y-x\|_2^2,$$
and consequently
$$\langle\nabla f(x)-\nabla f(y),x-y\rangle\ge\mu\|x-y\|_2^2.$$
thm-stochastic-gradient-strong-convex-di:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ have $L$-Lipschitz gradient for $L>0$ and be $\mu$-strongly convex in the strong-Jensen sense of [[def-strong-convex-composite-objective]] for $\mu>0$, with minimizer $x^\ast$ satisfying $\nabla f(x^\ast)=0$. Start the unconstrained update of [[def-stochastic-gradient-oracle-and-unconstrained-update]] at deterministic $x_0$, with
$$\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k),\qquad \mathbb E[\|G_k\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le M^2$$
almost surely for every $k$. Use $\alpha_0=1/\mu$ and $\alpha_k=1/(\mu(k+1))$ for $k\ge1$. Then for every $k\ge1$,
$$\mathbb E\|x_k-x^\ast\|_2^2\le\frac{M^2}{\mu^2 k},\qquad \mathbb E[f(x_k)-f(x^\ast)]\le\frac{LM^2}{2\mu^2 k}.$$
def-projected-stochastic-gradient-update:
## Definition

Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let $x_0\in C$. The Euclidean projection $P_C(y)$ is the unique nearest point to $y$ in $C$; its existence and equivalence with the proximal map of the indicator of $C$ are supplied by [[lem-prox-indicator-is-euclidean-projection]]. The indicator is zero on $C$ and $+\infty$ off $C$, as defined in [[def-indicator-function-of-closed-convex-set]]. For the filtration-adapted oracle of [[def-stochastic-gradient-oracle-and-unconstrained-update]], projected SGD takes, at each iteration $k$:

1. form $y_k=x_k-\alpha_kG_k$;
2. set $x_{k+1}=P_C(y_k)$.

The output is the next iterate, which lies in $C$. The procedure has no failure branch because the projection exists uniquely for every $y_k\in\mathbb R^d$ under the stated conditions. Its nonexpansiveness is not part of this definition; it is supplied by the proximal-map theorem when used in proofs.
thm-projected-stochastic-gradient-strong:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex. Let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable, and suppose $F=f+\iota_C$ is $\mu$-strongly convex for $\mu>0$ in the sense of [[def-strong-convex-composite-objective]], where $\iota_C$ is zero on $C$ and $+\infty$ off $C$ ([[def-indicator-function-of-closed-convex-set]]). Assume a minimizer $x^\ast\in C$ exists. Start projected SGD as in [[def-projected-stochastic-gradient-update]] from square-integrable $x_0\in C$, with
$$\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k),\qquad \mathbb E[\|G_k\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le M^2$$
almost surely for every $k$, where $M<\infty$. For deterministic stepsizes satisfying $0<\alpha_k\le1/(2\mu)$, $\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty$, and $\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty$, the iterates converge almost surely to $x^\ast$. The projection supplies stability, so no separate coercivity hypothesis is needed for this projected theorem.
thm-projected-stochastic-gradient-convex:
## Statement

Assume AC. Let $C\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, with diameter $D=\sup_{x,y\in C}\|x-y\|_2<\infty$. Let $f:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R$ be differentiable and convex, and assume a minimizer $x^\ast\in C$ exists. Start projected SGD at deterministic $x_0\in C$, with conditionally unbiased gradients, meaning $\mathbb E[G_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k)$ as in [[def-stochastic-gradient-oracle-and-unconstrained-update]], and
$$\mathbb E[\|G_k\|_2^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le G^2$$
almost surely for every $k$. For $N\ge1$, put $\bar x_N=N^{-1}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}x_k$. If $D,G>0$ and $\alpha_k=\alpha=D/(G\sqrt N)$ for $0\le k<N$, then
$$\mathbb E[f(\bar x_N)-f(x^\ast)]\le\frac{DG}{\sqrt N}.$$
If $D=0$ or $G=0$, the initial point is already optimal and the displayed bound holds with right side zero.
